Rokanuddin Mahmud, Senior Advocate instructed by Syed Mahbubar Rahman, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Petitioner 
Kamal-ul-Alam, Advocate, instructed by Mr. Zainul Abedin, Advocate-on-Record ----- For the Respondents

M. V. Fazlul Haque-3 represented by Md. Fazlul Huq ----- Petitioner
Vs.
Coral Shipping Lines Limited, represented by its Managing Director and other ----- Respondents
full_judgment:
2. Respondent No. 1, herein, as plaintiff (hereinafter referred to as the plaintiff filed the admiralty suit impleading the present petitioner and respondent Nos. 2 and respondent Nos. 4-6 as pro-forma defendants (though in law, there is frothing   principal and pro-forma defendants, hereinafter referred to as the defendant) for recovery of loss and damages amounting to taka 18,45,00,000.00 (eighteen crore forty five lac). The case of the plaintiff as made out in the plaint, in short is that on 04.07.2012, at about 10:30 (a.m. or p.m. nothing has been mentioned in the plaint), the plaintiffs oil tanker, M.T. Meher (Registration No. C-674) while carrying 1,87,522 liters of petrol and 562479 liters of diesel owned by defendant No. 6, Jamuna Oil Company from the Jamuna Jetty, Patenga, Chittagong to the depot of Jamuna Oil Company at Barisal, reached near village Sultani under Ulania Union, Mehendigonj Police Station near Barisal, defendant No. 1-cargo vessel M.T. Fazlul Haque-3 (M. No. 10503) hit the plaintiffs oil tanker, M.T. Meher from the rear side causing complete damage and Wreckage of the oil tanker, M.T. Meher causing loss and damage to the plaintiff amounting to taka 18,45,00,000.00 (eighteen crore forty five lac). In the suit, the plaintiff filed an application for arresting defendant No. 1, Vessel M.V. Fazlul Haque-3 (M. No. 10503) and the Admiralty Court by the order dated 05.08.2012 arrested the vessel. 

 3. Defendant Nos. 1 (the petitioner) and 3, on 04.11.2012, appeared in the suit and filed an application for release of the vessel from at rest, but did not take any stop to get the application heard. Then on 26.02.2013, a supplementary affidavit was filed in support of the application. It further appears that defendant Nos. 1 and 3 also filed an application on 11.03.2013 to pass an order to release the vessel without furnishing security, or, alternatively, to reduce the amount of security stating similar   facts. Both the applications were opposed by the plaintiff by filing written objection. The Admiralty Court upon hearing the applications rejected the same; hence this petition for leave to appeal. 

 4. Mr. Rokunuddin Mahmud, learned, appearing for the defendant-petitioner has tried to argue by referring to the documents filed with the additional paper book that the claim of the plaintiff in respect of the damage and compensation against the defendant-vessel is excessive .and the therefore, the High Court Division ought to have reduced the amount of security and ought to have also released the vessel from arrest. Mr. Mahmud has also tried to show by referring to the documents filed with the additional paper book that in fact, the oil tanker, which was allegedly his by the defendant-vessel, was salvaged in good condition, but the owners of the tanker in collusion with some dishonest people smuggled the petrol and the diesel contained therein, in the dead of night, amounting to taka 7 crore. He has further submitted that the oil tanker, which was allegedly damaged, was commissioned in 1983. The plaintiff is not entitled to the amount of the damage claimed, the High Court Division failed to consider the said fact in refusing the prayer made by the defendant for releasing the vessel from arrest, or, in the alternative to reduce the amount of security and thus fell into an error in passing the impugned order. 

 5. Mr. Kamal-ul Alam, learned Counsel, entering caveat on behalf of the plaintiff-respondent, on the other hand, has submitted that the claim made by the plaintiff on the account of damage and compensation in the suit is correct and based on facts and in deciding an interlocutory matter, there is no scope of entering into the dispute as to whether the amount claimed  by the plaintiff is excessive or not. He, by drawing our attention to the documents filed with the additional paper book (filed on behalf of the plaintiff-respondent), has submitted that the oil tanker, namely: M.T. Taher was completely damaged and it became scrap because of careless and negligent hit by defendant No. 1-Vessel and on the application filed by the plaintiff, the Admiralty Court allowed it to carry on the salvage work of the wreckage of the oil tanker and also to salvage the scraps of the wrecked vessel and accordingly, the auction notice was published in the newspaper and the same has already been sold in auction to auction-purchasers, namely: Md. Shaha Alom Manik, Md. Mizanur Rahman and Md. Nasiruddin which prima facie proved that the damage caused to the oil tanker as claimed by the plaintiff is correct and the High Court Division rightly refused to release defendant No. 1-vessel from arrest without furnishing security by the defendants and to reduce theme; amount of security money. 

 6. It is an admitted fact that there was a collision between the plaintiffs oil tanker-M.T. Meher and defendant No. 1-vessel and the oil tanker-M.T. Meher also sank because of the collision. Whether the oil tanker was completely damaged making it a scrap as claimed by the plaintiff and whether it was salvaged in good condition and whether the petrol and the diesel, which were in the oil tanker, could be recovered and whether those were smuggle by the owner of the oil tanker in collusion with others are purely questions of fact and those have to be decided at the trial on the evidence adduced by the parties. 

 7. On query. Mr. Rokanuddin Mahmud admitted that the documents filed with the additional paper book before this Division in support of his submission that the oil tanker-M.T. Meher did not suffer so much damage as claimed by the plaintiff and that the same was salvaged in good condition were not filed before the High Court Division during the hearing of the applications for releasing the vessel from arrest, or, alternatively to reduce the amount of security. Mr. Rokanuddin Mahmud could not also show with reference to any material on record that the order of arrest of the defendant-vessel by the Admiralty Court was passed arbitrarily and without any material on record, therefore, we do not find any prima facie illegality with the impugned order passed by the Admiralty Court calling for interference by that Division. However, the defendants shall be at liberty to file those documents (filed with the additional paper book) at the final hearing of the suit and if the documents are filed and proved showing that the oil tanker in question was an old one and was salvaged in good condition along with the petrol and diesel contained in the tanker after it had been hit by defendant No. 1-tanker; definitely the Admiralty Court shall consider those in deciding the merit of the claim of damage and compensation made by the plaintiff in the suit.
